claim: Large Bandwidth Tunnels are available only for VPN connections attached to a transit gateway or to Cloud WAN; they are not supported for virtual private gateway attachments.
question: Which target gateways support Large Bandwidth Tunnels for Site-to-Site VPN?

values.display: a transit gateway or to Cloud WAN

evidence.quote: Available only for VPN connections attached to a transit gateway or to Cloud WAN. Not supported for Virtual Private Gateway attachments.

claim: Both tunnels of a VPN connection must use the same bandwidth configuration: both 1.25 Gbps or both 5 Gbps.
question: Can the two tunnels of one Site-to-Site VPN connection have different bandwidth settings?

evidence.quote: Both tunnels of a VPN connection must use the same bandwidth configuration (both 1.25 Gbps or both 5 Gbps).

claim: In the requirements and limitations of Large Bandwidth Tunnels, accelerated VPN is not supported.
question: Can an accelerated Site-to-Site VPN connection use a Large Bandwidth Tunnel?
note: d12-009. Short quote: the scope (Large Bandwidth Tunnels, Requirements and limitations) stands in the headings above the line.

claim: You can modify the tunnel bandwidth of existing Site-to-Site VPN connections.
question: Can you change the tunnel bandwidth of an existing Site-to-Site VPN connection?

values.display: modify the tunnel bandwidth of existing VPN connections

evidence.quote: You can modify the tunnel bandwidth of existing VPN connections.

claim: On a transit gateway, ECMP can aggregate multiple VPN tunnels for higher bandwidth, but only when the VPN connection uses dynamic routing; ECMP is not supported with static routing.
question: Which routing type does ECMP over Site-to-Site VPN tunnels on a transit gateway need?

values.display: ECMP is not supported on VPN connections that use static routing

qualifiers.scope: per VPN connection on a transit gateway

evidence.quote: For Site-to-Site VPN connections on a transit gateway, you can use ECMP to get higher VPN bandwidth by aggregating multiple VPN tunnels. To use ECMP, the VPN connection must be configured for dynamic routing. ECMP is not supported on VPN connections that use static routing.

claim: IPv6 VPNs support the same throughput (Gbps and PPS), MTU and route limits as IPv4 VPNs, with no performance difference between IPv4 and IPv6 VPN connections.
question: Do IPv6 Site-to-Site VPN connections have different throughput, MTU or route limits than IPv4?

values.display: same throughput (Gbps and PPS), MTU, and route limits

evidence.quote: IPv6 VPNs support the same throughput (Gbps and PPS), MTU, and route limits as IPv4 VPNs. There are no performance differences between IPv4 and IPv6 VPN connections.

claim: Site-to-Site VPN supports a maximum transmission unit (MTU) of 1446 bytes and a corresponding maximum segment size (MSS) of 1406 bytes.
question: What MTU and MSS does a Site-to-Site VPN support?

evidence.quote: Site-to-Site VPN supports a maximum transmission unit (MTU) of 1446 bytes and a corresponding maximum segment size (MSS) of 1406 bytes.

note: d12-013. The Large Bandwidth Tunnel requirements bullet says MTU limit remains 1500 bytes; recorded as a source disagreement, not stored as a fact.

claim: In the MTU section of the Site-to-Site VPN quotas, jumbo frames are not supported.
question: Does a Site-to-Site VPN connection support jumbo frames?
note: d12-013. Short quote: scope stands in the MTU section heading above.

claim: A Site-to-Site VPN connection does not support Path MTU Discovery.
question: Does a Site-to-Site VPN connection support Path MTU Discovery?

values.display: does not support Path MTU Discovery

evidence.quote: A Site-to-Site VPN connection does not support Path MTU Discovery.

claim: Both accelerated and unassociated connections count towards the total Site-to-Site VPN connections per Region quota.
question: Do accelerated and unassociated VPN connections count towards the VPN connections per Region quota?

values.display: count towards the total Site-to-Site VPN connections per Region quota

evidence.quote: Both Accelerated and Unassociated connections count towards the total Site-to-Site VPN connections per Region quota.

claim: You can attach one virtual private gateway to a VPC at a time; to connect the same Site-to-Site VPN connection to multiple VPCs, AWS recommends a transit gateway.
question: How many virtual private gateways can be attached to a VPC at a time, and what does AWS recommend for several VPCs?

values.display: one virtual private gateway to a VPC at a time

evidence.quote: You can attach one virtual private gateway to a VPC at a time. To connect the same Site-to-Site VPN connection to multiple VPCs, we recommend that you explore using a transit gateway instead.

claim: For a Site-to-Site VPN connection with BGP, the BGP session resets if you advertise more routes than the maximum for the gateway type; with static routes you cannot add more than 100 static routes.
question: What happens when a customer gateway advertises more routes than the Site-to-Site VPN maximum?

evidence.quote: For a VPN connection with Static routes, you will not be able to add more than 100 static routes. For a VPN connection with BGP, the BGP session will reset if you attempt to advertise more than the maximum for the gateway type.
